findings.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed property keys from Zod schema objects that evaluate to '[object Object]' at runtime, creating a literal key instead of a wildcard key schema, so expiry fields and arbitrary properties are not validated as intended

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response object when credential sharing is enabled, but callers expect different return types (Google Calendar accesses res.data, Hubspot expects a HubspotToken, Zoho expects AxiosResponse), causing runtime failures across multiple adapters
.env.example comment says encryption key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but the suggested command 'openssl rand -base64 24' generates only 24 bytes, producing an invalid key

When credential sharing is enabled, minimumTokenResponseSchema strips refresh_token from output and the code unconditionally sets refresh_token to the literal placeholder string 'refresh_token', corrupting the credential and breaking subsequent token refresh attempts

Zoho Bigin CalendarService passes credentialId as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens while all other adapters pass credential.userId, causing a potential ReferenceError or wrong value passed to the credential sync endpoint
No HTTP method restriction in app-credential.ts webhook handler — GET, DELETE, or any other method will proceed to read and parse req.body, causing errors or unintended behavior

symmetricDecrypt() and subsequent JSON.parse() on decrypted keys in app-credential.ts are not wrapped in try-catch, causing unhandled 500 errors with no diagnostic response

minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts is malformed — computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to literal string '[object Object]', overwriting each other and silently dropping real fields like expiry_date and refresh_token

parseRefreshTokenResponse() returns the full safeParse result object { success, data, error } but it is stored directly as credential key in Google CalendarService.ts, persisting incorrect object structure to the database and breaking downstream credential reads

Zoho Bigin CalendarService.ts passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens instead of credential.userId, causing sync endpoint to look up the wrong user when credential sharing is enabled

Salesforce CalendarService.ts does not use refreshOAuthTokens like all other updated services, so token refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint entirely when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, making the feature silently non-functional for Salesforce

Salesforce CalendarService.ts runs the token refresh block unconditionally during service construction instead of only when the access token is expired, causing an extra HTTP call for every calendar operation

Salesforce CalendarService.ts error handling checks response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok or response.status, which is server-dependent and may be empty or localized, producing false positives or false negatives

refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns a raw Response object from fetch() when credential sharing is enabled, but callers in Hubspot, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin, and Google Calendar expect different object types, causing runtime breakage
No response.ok check on the credential sync endpoint response in refreshOAuthTokens.ts, so a 4xx/5xx response is passed through without error and fails opaquely during response parsing

No authentication header or shared secret is sent in the fetch() to the credential sync endpoint in refreshOAuthTokens.ts, allowing any party who can reach the endpoint to request credential refresh for any user

In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts when credential sharing is enabled, Zod strips unknown keys so refresh_token is always undefined, causing the code to always set refresh_token to the literal dummy string "refresh_token", breaking future token refreshes

.env.example comment for CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY states it must be 32 bytes but the suggested command openssl rand -base64 24 generates only 24 random bytes, causing self-hosters to create an undersized key

In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts, the change from ${appConfig.slug} to a hardcoded zoho-bigin in the redirect URI is unrelated to OAuth credential sync and is scope drift that belongs in a separate PR

In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, a new token-refresh flow bypasses the refreshOAuthTokens utility that every other integration uses, creating inconsistency with the PR's stated intent

In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the utility returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but callers expect integration-specific shapes (HubspotToken SDK object, axios response for Zoho, res.data for Google, etc.), breaking the credential-sync path for most integrations

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed property keys from Zod schema objects that evaluate to '[object Object]' at runtime, creating a literal key instead of a wildcard key schema, so expiry fields and arbitrary properties are not validated as intended

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(), })`. Those computed keys are evaluated immediately when the object literal is created, and `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object whose `.toString()` is not a wildcard key specifier; it will produce a concrete string (typically `"[object Object]"` or similar). That means the schema ends up with a literal property name rather than validating “any numeric field” or “any extra property”, so expiry/arbitrary fields are not validated as intended (the correct approach would be `z.record(...)` / `.catchall(...)`).

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` does not check `req.method` (e.g., only allow POST). As written, any HTTP method that includes the correct secret header will reach `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns a raw Response object from fetch() when credential sharing is enabled, but callers in Hubspot, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin, and Google Calendar expect different object types, causing runtime breakage

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it returns the raw `Response` from `fetch(...)`. But some callers expect a non-fetch shape:
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` treats the return as a Google auth refresh result and does `const token = res?.data;` and then reads `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and this will break at runtime.
- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In the enabled branch this would actually be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, so subsequent property access on `hubspotRefreshToken` will break.
The finding’s mention of Zoho/Zoho Bigin isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the core issue (returning a `Response` where callers expect different types) is clearly introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No response.ok check on the credential sync endpoint response in refreshOAuthTokens.ts, so a 4xx/5xx response is passed through without error and fails opaquely during response parsing

No authentication header or shared secret is sent in the fetch() to the credential sync endpoint in refreshOAuthTokens.ts, allowing any party who can reach the endpoint to request credential refresh for any user

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only a `URLSearchParams` body containing `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` and no authentication header/secret/token/signature. The diff also introduces webhook secret env vars (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`) for an inbound webhook route, but nothing analogous is used for this outbound credential-sync request. So as written, the sync endpoint cannot verify the caller, and anyone who can reach that endpoint could make the same request payload for arbitrary `calcomUserId`/`appSlug`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts when credential sharing is enabled, Zod strips unknown keys so refresh_token is always undefined, causing the code to always set refresh_token to the literal dummy string "refresh_token", breaking future token refreshes

.env.example comment for CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY states it must be 32 bytes but the suggested command openssl rand -base64 24 generates only 24 random bytes, causing self-hosters to create an undersized key

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds comments for `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` saying it "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" but then suggests generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces 24 random bytes (192 bits) before base64 encoding. That contradicts the stated 32-byte requirement and could mislead self-hosters into creating a key that doesn't meet the documented size requirement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts, the change from ${appConfig.slug} to a hardcoded zoho-bigin in the redirect URI is unrelated to OAuth credential sync and is scope drift that belongs in a separate PR

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references a change in `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts` (from `${appConfig.slug}` to hardcoded `zoho-bigin` in a redirect URI), but that file and change do not appear anywhere in the provided diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, a new token-refresh flow bypasses the refreshOAuthTokens utility that every other integration uses, creating inconsistency with the PR's stated intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff snippet for `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` only shows new imports (`z` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) and the addition of `salesforceTokenSchema`, but it does not show any token-refresh logic being added/changed, nor any place where `refreshOAuthTokens` would be expected/required. adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the utility returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but callers expect integration-specific shapes (HubspotToken SDK object, axios response for Zoho, res.data for Google, etc.), breaking the credential-sync path for most integrations
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: when credential sync/sharing is enabled, the refresh helper returns a raw fetch Response, but multiple integration callers (e.g., Google expecting res.data, Hubspot expecting a HubspotToken, etc.) assume an integration-specific token/response shape, leading to runtime errors unless the return type or call sites are adjusted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line ~91), parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParseReturnType wrapper but the code stores it directly as key in Prisma, so the DB receives { success, data } instead of the parsed credential object

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the code changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the parsed credential object) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new in diff) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data }`) rather than `data` (it even checks `success` then returns `refreshTokenResponse` directly). That value is then written to Prisma as `data: { key }`, so the DB would receive the wrapper object instead of the credential payload shape previously stored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts (lines 6-11), minimumTokenResponseSchema uses z.string().toString() as computed keys which produce a constant string causing key collision, and Zod strips unknown keys by default so fields like expiry_date, scope, and token_type are silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, the computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are evaluated immediately to a single constant string (whatever `toString()` returns for a Zod type, e.g. "[object Object]"), not an index signature. The second entry will overwrite the first due to identical key strings, so this schema does not actually express “any numeric property”/“any other property”. As a result, fields like `expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type`, etc. are not part of the schema and Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so those properties will be removed from `refreshTokenResponse.data` when `safeParse` succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts (lines 24-26), when parsed data lacks refresh_token the code sets it to the literal string "refresh_token" instead of preserving the real one, breaking subsequent refreshes
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same bug: when refresh_token is missing in the parsed OAuth response, the function assigns the literal string "refresh_token" (hardcoded) instead of a valid token value, which breaks subsequent refresh flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the handler never checks req.method, allowing GET/DELETE/PUT requests with the matching secret to be processed and mutate credentials

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` performs credential create/update purely based on header secret + parsed `req.body`, but it never gates on `req.method` (e.g., only allowing POST). As written, any HTTP method (PUT/PATCH/etc.) that Next.js provides a parsed body for and includes the matching secret header will execute the same mutation logic. Even for methods like GET, the handler still attempts to `parse(req.body)` rather than returning 405, which is incorrect behavior for a mutating webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts (lines ~22, ~57), appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) can throw but are not wrapped in try/catch, causing unhandled 500s instead of structured 4xx responses for invalid payloads

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (zod `parse` throws on invalid payload) and later does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (both `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` can throw on bad ciphertext/key or invalid JSON). There is no surrounding `try/catch` or error handling in the handler, so malformed requests will bubble an exception and Next.js will return a generic 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts (lines 6-7), decodeOAuthState is imported via a convoluted ../oauth/decodeOAuthState path instead of ./decodeOAuthState, suggesting a mechanical unreviewed refactor

adjudication.rationale: In the renamed file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts`, the import `../oauth/decodeOAuthState` is redundant/convoluted but it still correctly resolves to the same module (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts`) because it goes up one level to `_utils/` and back into `oauth/`. The diff does not show a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect caused by this path; the claim about an “unreviewed refactor” is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/lib/constants.ts (lines 102-103), APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to the string value of the encryption key (or undefined) instead of a boolean, leaking secret material into a broadly-imported constant

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not modify or show `packages/lib/constants.ts`, nor does it show how `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is computed. The new/changed code only *imports* that constant from `@calcom/lib/constants` and adds new env vars in `.env.example`. Therefore the claim that it "evaluates to the string value of the encryption key" and leaks secret material via a broadly-imported constant is not verifiable from this diff and appears to be speculation about code not included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to '[object Object]', creating a broken schema that does not validate an expiry field, does not passthrough (stripping unknown keys like refresh_token, expiry_date, instance_url), and does not enforce the intended constraint, causing all non-access_token fields to be lost from parsed credentials when credential sharing is enabled

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed property keys like `[z.string().toString()]`. `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object, so `.toString()` does not create a dynamic key matcher; it becomes a single literal property name (effectively something like `"[object Object]"`). As a result, the schema only truly requires `access_token` and does not correctly validate/require any expiry field. Also, because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default (no `.passthrough()`), fields like `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc. from the real response will be dropped from `refreshTokenResponse.data` when credential sharing is enabled. The subsequent `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { ... }` will then always run even if the response included a refresh token, confirming the data-loss behavior described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google CalendarService assigns the full SafeParseReturnType from parseRefreshTokenResponse instead of .data, persisting { success: true, data: {...} } instead of the parsed credentials, corrupting stored tokens on every refresh

When refresh_token is missing or stripped by the broken schema, it is set to the literal string 'refresh_token' as a sentinel value, which is persisted to the DB and sent to OAuth providers as a real refresh token, causing authentication failures

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly mutates parsed token data: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. This means any refresh-token response/schema that does not include `refresh_token` (common for OAuth refresh flows, and explicitly allowed by `minimumTokenResponseSchema` when credential sync is enabled) will have the refresh token overwritten with the literal string. In `Office365CalendarService`, the returned object is merged into `o365AuthCredentials` via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` and then persisted with `prisma.credential.update`, so the sentinel value can be stored in DB and later used as the actual `refresh_token` in subsequent refresh calls, causing authentication failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw Response from fetch() when credential sharing is on, but callers expect provider-specific types (HubspotToken object, Axios response, etc.), causing undefined property access, broken credentials, or runtime errors

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` when sharing is enabled, i.e., a raw `Response` object. But multiple callers in the diff expect non-`Response` provider-specific return shapes:
- `GoogleCalendarService`: assigns `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then does `const token = res?.data;` and reads `token.access_token`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and this will throw when accessing `token.access_token`.
- `HubspotCalendarService`: types the result as `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`), but in the sharing-enabled branch it will actually be a `Response`, so downstream property access on the token object will break.
Other usages that already expect a `Response` (e.g., Office365/Lark) are fine, but the inconsistency makes the finding a real defect introduced/visible in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race condition in find-then-create/update credential flow: findFirst + conditional create/update with no unique constraint and no transaction allows concurrent webhook calls to create duplicate credentials or interleave updates; missing @@unique([userId, appId]) is the root data-model defect

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts) the code does a non-atomic read-then-write sequence: prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } }) followed by either credential.update({ where: { id } }) or credential.create({ data: { userId, appId, ... } }). Without wrapping this in a transaction and/or using an upsert on a unique key, concurrent webhook requests for the same (userId, appId) can both observe “no credential” and both create, producing duplicates, or interleave updates unpredictably. The diff itself shows no transaction and no upsert, so the race is verifiable. However, the claim that a missing @@unique([userId, appId]) is the “root data-model defect” is not directly verifiable from this diff because the Prisma schema/constraints are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Timing-unsafe webhook secret comparison using !== instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, vulnerable to timing side-channel attacks

adjudication.rationale:
In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret is verified via a direct inequality check:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

This is a normal string/primitive comparison (`!==`) and is not designed to be constant-time. For secret validation, this can leak information via timing differences (in principle) compared to using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on buffers. So the finding points to a concrete issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled Zod .parse() throws ZodError on malformed input, producing a 500 instead of a 400 and potentially leaking schema details in the stack trace; should use safeParse with structured error response

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the request body is validated with `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` without any try/catch. `zod.parse()` throws a `ZodError` on malformed input, which in a Next.js API handler will propagate and result in a 500 response rather than a controlled 400-series error. This is directly verifiable from the diff and aligns with the finding’s claim about unhandled parse errors (safeParse/explicit error handling would avoid that).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Decrypted credential payload from JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is stored directly as the credential key with no schema validation, allowing malformed or attacker-controlled data to be persisted as a credential

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is obtained via `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` and then written directly to the DB as `data: { key: keys }` in both `prisma.credential.update` and `prisma.credential.create`. There is no schema/Zod validation of the decrypted JSON structure before persistence (unlike other credential flows in the diff that use `googleCredentialSchema` / `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, etc.). This makes it possible for malformed/unexpected JSON (whoever can call the webhook with the secret) to be stored as a credential key and potentially break downstream code that assumes a specific shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refresh does not use refreshOAuthTokens, so Salesforce credentials are never synced via the endpoint, yet parseRefreshTokenResponse still applies the broken minimumTokenResponseSchema globally, stripping instance_url, signature, scope, etc. and breaking the jsforce Connection

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce code uses response.statusText for error checking instead of response.ok or response.status, which is unreliable as statusText is a human-readable string that varies by server/proxy

adjudication.rationale: The provided diff does not show any Salesforce code using `response.statusText` for error checking. adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce token is always refreshed on initialization with no expiry check, wastefully calling the token endpoint during construction without checking if the current access token is still valid, increasing latency and risking rate-limiting

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any Salesforce initialization logic that refreshes tokens, nor any construction-time call to a token endpoint. The only visible Salesforce changes are importing `zod`, adding `parseRefreshTokenResponse` import, and defining a `salesforceTokenSchema`. adjudication_records.issue_text: fetch() to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no AbortController/timeout so a hanging endpoint blocks all OAuth refreshes indefinitely, and the response is returned without checking response.ok, so HTTP errors propagate as malformed data

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` without any `AbortController`/`signal` or other timeout mechanism, so the promise can hang for an unbounded time if the endpoint is slow/unresponsive. The function also returns the `Response` directly without checking `response.ok` (or otherwise validating status), meaning non-2xx responses are not rejected here and can flow to callers as if they were successful responses, leading to downstream parsing/usage errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to the encryption-key string or empty/undefined instead of true/false; should use Boolean(...); also the flag does not include CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT so the enabled state and sync-path activation are inconsistent, silently falling through to local provider when endpoint is missing

adjudication.rationale:
The diff only *imports* `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` from `@calcom/lib/constants`; it does not show how it’s computed. Therefore the claim that it “evaluates to the encryption-key string or empty/undefined instead of true/false” is not verifiable from this diff.

Also, the new helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) explicitly gate sync behavior on **both** `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Falling back to the local provider when the endpoint is missing appears to be intentional behavior in the added code, not a clear defect introduced by the diff.

The webhook handler’s initial check uses only `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, but that doesn’t create the specific inconsistency alleged (and sync-path activation is correctly guarded elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zoho-bigin passes credentialId where userId is expected in refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the credential's DB id instead of calcomUserId, looking up the wrong entity
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that refreshOAuthTokens is being called with credentialId instead of the expected userId, causing the sync endpoint to look up the wrong entity. This is the same underlying bug described in the golden comment (incorrect user lookup breaking credential sync).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unnecessary full-row load via prisma.user.findUnique selecting all scalar columns when only existence is needed; should use select: { id: true }

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code does `await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } });` and only uses the result for an existence check (`if (!user)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead .success checks after parseRefreshTokenResponse are unreachable since parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on !success, and the Office365 change removed the console.error that logged the Zod error and raw provider response, replacing it with a generic error message that destroys diagnostic information

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` uses `schema.safeParse(...)` (or `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)`) and then immediately `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `!refreshTokenResponse.success`. Therefore any later logic that branches on `.success` is unreachable/pointless. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code still does `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)`, but `tokenResponse.success` will always be true if execution reaches that line.

Also, the Office365 code previously logged detailed diagnostics on Zod failure (`tokenResponse.error` and the raw `responseJson`). That block was removed, and failures will now surface only via the generic thrown Error from `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which does lose the Zod error and provider response context at this call site. This loss of diagnostic information is directly observable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No replay protection on webhook endpoint: validates only a static shared secret with no timestamp, nonce, or HMAC signature, allowing captured valid requests to be replayed to overwrite credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the only authenticity check is `req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] === CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, i.e., a static shared-secret header. The handler then decrypts `reqBody.keys` and performs `credential.update`/`credential.create` with no timestamp, nonce, request id, signature (HMAC), or other anti-replay mechanism. As a result, any previously captured valid request (header + body) can be resent later to re-apply/overwrite the stored credential (e.g., replaying an older captured payload could restore older keys). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` which evaluate to literal 'ZodString' and do not validate the expiry field as the comment claims

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JavaScript this evaluates the expression once and uses its *string result* as a literal property name (e.g., "ZodString" / "[object Object]"), not as an index-signature/wildcard for “any string key”. Zod `z.object({...})` does not interpret this as “any numeric field is allowed”; it will instead require that exact literal key to exist, so real token responses with fields like `expires_in`/`expiry_date` won’t satisfy the schema, making the parsing/validation incorrect (and likely always failing) when the minimum schema path is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When refresh_token is missing it is set to the literal string 'refresh_token', overwriting the real refresh token with garbage and permanently breaking future refreshes
parseRefreshTokenResponse returns full SafeParseReturnType { success, data, error } but Google Calendar code stores it directly as credential key, persisting wrong object shape to database

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function runs `schema.safeParse(...)` (or `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)`) and returns `refreshTokenResponse` directly. That return value is a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object with shape `{ success, data, error }`, not the parsed credential payload itself.

In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new code does:
```ts
const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);
await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } });
```
This would persist the safe-parse wrapper object into `credential.key`, changing the stored schema from the expected credentials object to `{success, data, error}`. That is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff (and contrasts with Office365 which treats the return as a SafeParseReturnType and uses `.data`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response in sync mode but already-parsed objects in non-sync mode, breaking Hubspot and Lark callers that expect typed/parsed objects
matched_golden_ids: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: in sync mode refreshOAuthTokens yields a raw fetch Response instead of a parsed object, so callers expecting a consistent shape (e.g., accessing res.data/access_token) will get undefined and can crash at runtime. The candidate generalizes the impact to specific callers but matches the inconsistency described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce token-refresh fetch runs unconditionally without gating on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED feature flag, changing behavior for non-sync users

adjudication.rationale: The diff segment for `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` only shows new imports (`z`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) and addition of a `salesforceTokenSchema`. It does not show any token-refresh fetch logic being added/changed, nor any place where gating on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` would be expected but missing. adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse typed to accept schema: z.ZodTypeAny but returns safeParse result without unwrapping, creating inconsistent contract that causes Google caller bug

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the *result of* `schema.safeParse(...)` / `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)` (a `{ success, data|error }` object), not the parsed `data` value. This creates an inconsistent contract with prior callers that expected a parsed credential object (like `schema.parse(...)`). The diff shows a concrete bug in `GoogleCalendarService`: it changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `key` directly into Prisma as `data: { key }`. That will store the Zod safeParse wrapper instead of the credential payload, breaking expected credential shape. Other callers (e.g. Office365) treat the return as a safeParse result, highlighting the inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-constant-time webhook secret comparison using `!==` instead of `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, enabling timing attacks to recover the webhook secret byte-by-byte

adjudication.rationale:
The new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` validates the shared secret with a direct inequality check:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

This is a byte-by-byte/string comparison that is not guaranteed to be constant-time, so it can theoretically leak information via timing differences compared to using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on normalized `Buffer`s. The issue is directly present in the diff and affects an authentication check guarding the endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken Zod validation schema in `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` where `z.string().toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"`, causing all non-access_token fields to be stripped and validation to be bypassed when credential sharing is enabled

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. The computed keys are evaluated immediately as strings; `z.string().toString()` (and the optional variant) will not create “any string key” validation, it will produce a single literal property name (typically `"[object Object]"`), and the second one likely overwrites the first due to identical key strings. As a result, when credential sharing is enabled, `safeParse(response)` only validates `access_token` and otherwise treats real token fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, etc.) as unknown keys that Zod `z.object` strips by default, effectively bypassing the intended validation/shape enforcement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Insecure refresh_token fallback sets the literal string `"refresh_token"` when the field is missing, corrupting stored credentials and permanently breaking OAuth integrations

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly does `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. In the credential-sharing path it validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which doesn’t require a real `refresh_token`), then injects this literal placeholder. Call sites like Office365 then merge the parsed data into persisted credentials (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` followed by `prisma.credential.update`), which can overwrite a previously valid refresh token with the string "refresh_token". That corrupts stored credentials and can break future refresh flows if the normal OAuth refresh path is later used (e.g., credential sync disabled/misconfigured).
